name: Large Language Model
description: Transformer-based intelligence that learns language structure through self-supervised prediction on vast corpora. Attention mechanisms allow dynamic relational binding across sequence positions. Exhibits emergent reasoning, in-context learning, and co-creative capacity at sufficient scale, bridging symbolic and sub-symbolic cognition.

core_attributes.pattern: next-token prediction, contextual embedding, attention routing

training_paradigm: self-supervised next-token prediction with RLHF alignment
computational_substrate: distributed GPU/TPU clusters, massive parameter spaces

scope.definition: Performance advantage of self-attention over RNN/LSTM baselines on long-context tasks — measured as BLEU/ROUGE score improvement on summarization tasks with context length >2000 tokens.

evidence.source: Vaswani et al. (2017) 'Attention is all you need', NeurIPS; Dai et al. (2019) 'Transformer-XL', ACL.
cross_domain_examples: Transformer BLEU score on WMT14 En-De: 28.4 vs LSTM 26.3 — 2.1 point improvement on long sequences
self-attention O(n²) complexity enables full-context integration impossible for sequential RNNs
biological attention: prefrontal cortex gating of sensory input — selective processing analogue

scope.falsifiability: If LSTM architectures with adequate memory (N²-capacity) achieve statistically identical performance to transformers on long-context benchmarks, self-attention is not the relevant difference.
scope.measurement_limits: Self-attention quadratic complexity becomes computationally limiting for context >10k tokens — sparse/linear attention variants trade quality for scalability. Benchmark scores depend heavily on training data and scale.

scope.definition: Few-shot learning accuracy of large language models — performance on novel classification tasks using k=5 examples in context, without gradient updates, compared to fine-tuned smaller model baseline.

evidence.source: Brown et al. (2020) 'Language models are few-shot learners', NeurIPS (GPT-3); Min et al. (2022) 'Rethinking the role of demonstrations', EMNLP.
cross_domain_examples: GPT-3 175B: 5-shot SuperGLUE 71.8 vs fine-tuned BERT 89.3 — ICL approaches but doesn't match fine-tuning
ICL performance scales with model size — GPT-3 175B vs GPT-2 1.5B shows 40% relative improvement
human few-shot learning: classification from 5 examples — cognitive analogue with ~0.85 accuracy on novel categories

scope.falsifiability: If ICL performance is statistically indistinguishable from random labeling on standard few-shot benchmarks for a given model size, the examples-in-context are not being used for task inference.
scope.measurement_limits: ICL accuracy is highly sensitive to example selection, label formatting, and task type. Some tasks show near-random ICL performance at any scale. Performance measured on distribution-matched few-shot sets.

scope.definition: Semantic similarity preservation in LLM token embeddings — Spearman rank correlation between human-rated semantic similarity scores and cosine similarity of token embedding vectors on STS-B benchmark.

evidence.source: Mikolov et al. (2013) 'Distributed representations of words', NeurIPS (Word2Vec); Devlin et al. (2018) 'BERT', NAACL 2019.
cross_domain_examples: BERT contextual embeddings: STS-B Spearman correlation 0.87-0.92 vs human judgments
Word2Vec: famous 'king-man+woman=queen' analogy accuracy 0.70 on analogy evaluation sets
distributional semantics hypothesis: words in similar contexts have similar meanings — underlying theory

scope.falsifiability: If cosine similarity of token embeddings shows no correlation with human semantic similarity ratings (Spearman R<0.20) on STS-B, the embedding space does not capture semantic similarity.
scope.measurement_limits: STS-B correlation measures sentence-level similarity — individual token embeddings show weaker correlation. Polysemy is a known limitation: 'bank' (river vs financial) gets single embedding in static methods.

scope.definition: Quality of LLM-human co-creative output — rated improvement (human evaluation, 1-5 scale) of creative works (story, code, design) produced with LLM assistance vs baseline human-only in same time allocation.

evidence.source: Ippolito et al. (2022) 'Creative writing with an AI collaborator', EMNLP; Chakrabarty et al. (2023) 'Art or artifice? Large language models and the false promise of creativity', CHI.
cross_domain_examples: human writers with AI assistance: 0.6 point improvement on 5-point creativity scale vs solo writing
programming with GitHub Copilot: 55% faster task completion, 0.85 code quality parity with AI assistance
human-AI art collaboration: judges rate AI-assisted pieces higher in technical execution, lower in originality

scope.falsifiability: If blinded evaluators rate LLM-assisted creative work indistinguishably from human-only work at equivalent quality levels, AI assistance is not improving co-creative output quality.
scope.measurement_limits: Improvement depends on task type — technical creative tasks (code, structured writing) show stronger LLM benefit. Open-ended artistic tasks show mixed results with potential homogenization of style.
